patch_description:
The current program uses six cube--axis initializations, Gaussian perturbations of scale 0.115, five soft-min/soft-max gradient phases with powers 4 through 64, and three accept-only active-contact polishing stages.

This version changes the search configuration in several ways:

- Uses seven axial-radius basins, including values closer to the cube circumradius regime.
- Uses a longer but more concentrated continuation schedule through powers 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 96.
- Scales soft-min and soft-max weights relative to the current minimum and maximum distance, improving numerical conditioning at high powers.
- Uses momentum in the smooth phase to avoid repeatedly cancelling useful coordinated motion.
- Uses weighted active-set contact forces rather than uniform contact averaging: pairs closest to the current minimum and farthest from the current diameter receive greater force.
- Adds deterministic adaptive coordinate mutation search after the best continuous solution is found. Mutation scales shrink or expand according to acceptance rate, helping resolve contact-switching barriers that gradient-only polishing can miss.
- Finishes with a tighter active-set pass while always retaining the best exact squared distance ratio.

The returned array remains deterministic, finite, and has shape `(14, 3)`.
